dataset.description: Johann Friedrich Hartknoch was a notable 18th-century German bookseller and publisher who played a significant role in the dissemination of Enlightenment thought and German philosophy. Born in East Prussia, Hartknoch became best known for his publishing house in Riga, which was instrumental in promoting the works of prominent figures such as Immanuel Kant, Johann Gottfried Herder, and Johann Georg Hamann. Hartknoch's publishing career coincided with a period of intense intellectual activity in German-speaking Europe. His publishing house became a vital conduit for philosophical and theological discourse. He is perhaps most famously remembered for being the original publisher of Kant's 'Critique of Pure Reason' (1781)

distribution.title: The dataset of books published by Johann Friedrich Hartknoch was collected to support scholarly analysis of his contributions to Enlightenment-era publishing and intellectual history. The purpose of this data collection is to systematically document Hartknoch’s publishing activity, including authors, titles, publication years, and subject areas, in order to gain insights into his role in shaping the intellectual discourse of late 18th-century Europe. The dataset was compiled from the information stored on the repositary of the National Library of Latvia.

dataset.title: Publishing history of Johann Friedrich Hartknoch

dmp.description: Over the 500 years, the history of Latvian books has proven and continues to prove that the book has a significant role in the processes of political, social, cultural, economical change. The dissemination of books has been important in the changes of thinking, circulation of knowledge and building the value systems. The perspective through books can increase the knowledge of these processes significantly because it raises the issue of the dynamics of various forms of identity at several levels: both in regional, religious and social groups, and on a wider scale by bringing attention to Latvia's Western and European cultural orientation. Located on the border between historical Eastern and Western regions, Latvian culture has been subject to various, often competing influences, but has convincingly joined the European cultural space. The project will address the question: in which forms has the development of the printed word influenced this process and does so today. (No. lzp-2023/1-0263)
dmp.title: Book and Society in Latvia: European Dimension and Cultural Transformations
